$comment: The judge's window onto the desk. Alpaca's official MCP server, pointed at
the competition paper account, so the running system can be interrogated in
plain English: what is open, what did it refuse, what is the account doing.
Execution does NOT go through here. Every order HALFSPREAD places is an
Alpaca CLI invocation recorded verbatim in data/journal/*.jsonl, so each one
can be read and replayed by hand. The CLI is the agent's hands; MCP is the
window. Keys are read from the environment and are never committed - copy
.env.example to .env and fill it in, or export them in your shell.
Toolsets are limited to account, trading, assets and news, but be clear about
what that does and does not buy: verified 2026-09-03, the server still exposes
35 tools including place_option_order, because the order-placing tools are
built-in overrides rather than spec-driven operations the toolset filter
reaches. So this is a read-only window by convention and by how HALFSPREAD is
wired, NOT by enforcement. The guarantee that COMP is only traded deliberately
lives in agent/execute.py, which refuses the competition account without an
explicit arming token, and in the journal, where every order that ever reached
the broker is recorded as a replayable CLI invocation.
